<h>Reading 3</h>
From the Holy Gospel according to Matthew
<r>Matt 7:15-21</r>
<c>A</c>t that time, Jesus said unto His disciples: Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves. And so on.

Homily by St. Hilary, Bishop of Poitiers.
<r>Comment. on Matth. ch. vi.</r>
<c>T</c>he Lord here warneth us that we must rate the worth of soft words and seeming meekness, by the fruits which they that manifest such things bring forth in their works, and that we should look, in order to see what a man is, not at his professions, but at his deeds. For there are many in whom sheep's clothing is but a mask to hide wolfish ravening. But “Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles? Even so, every good tree bringeth forth good fruit, but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit.” Thus, the Lord teacheth us, is it with men also; evil men bring not forth good fruits, and hereby are we to know them. Lip-service alone winneth not the kingdom of heaven, nor is every one that saith unto Christ: “Lord, Lord,” an heir thereof.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

b.fbb35420ae:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>J</c>uly 5th 2027, the 1st day of the Moon,
<h>O</h>n the morrow we keep the Feast of St. Anthony Mary Zaccaria, Confessor, founder of the Clerks Regular of St. Paul, a man illustrious for every virtue, and famous for miracles. Leo XIII enrolled his name among those of the Saints. His body is reverenced at Milan, in the Church of St. Barnabas.
<h>U</h>pon the same 5th day of July, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy martyr Zoe, the wife of the blessed martyr Nicostratus. She was praying at the grave of the blessed Apostle Peter when she was arrested by the persecutor under the Emperor Diocletian, and committed to a dark prison. In the end she was hung on a tree by her neck and hair, and a thick smoke made below her, and so, constantly confessing the Lord, gave up the Ghost.
<h>A</h>t Jerusalem, holy Athanasius, Deacon [of the Church of Rome.]
<h>H</h>e was seized by the heretics regarding the holy council of Chalcedon, [held in the year 451,] and after he had been tried with all kinds of torments, was at length slain with the sword, [in the year 452.]
<h>I</h>n Syria, the holy martyr Domitius, [in the year 363,] who by his power doth many kindnesses unto the dwellers there.
<h>I</h>n Sicily, the holy martyrs Agathon and Triphina.
<h>A</h>t Timisoara, on the Black Sea, the holy martyrs Marinus, Theodotus, and Sedophas.
<h>A</h>t Cyrene, in Libya, the holy martyr Cyrilla, [in the year 310.] In the persecution under Diocletian live embers mixed with incense were laid upon her hand, and she held them there for a long while, lest, if she jerked away the live coals, she should seem to have offered the incense, when she was most cruelly mangled, and so passed away to Christ her Bridegroom adorned with her own blood.
<h>A</h>t Trier, the holy Confessor Numerian, [Bishop of that see, in the year 657.]
<h>A</h>t San Severino, in Picenum, the holy Virgin Philumena, [sixth century.]
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

b.1a22b7235d:
<h>Regula vel Evangelium</h>
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
May the divine assistance ✠ remain with us always.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>t</c>o Matthew
<r>Matt 7:15-21</r>
<c>A</c>t that time, Jesus said to His disciples: Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravenous wolves. By their fruits you will know them. Do men gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles? Even so, every good tree bears good fruit, but the bad tree bears bad fruit. A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, nor can a bad tree bear good fruit. Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire. Therefore, by their fruits you will know them. Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ shall enter the kingdom of heaven; but he who does the will of My Father in heaven shall enter the kingdom of heaven.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
Commemoration of the deceased Brethren, Sisters, Relations and Benefactors of our Order.
Requiéscant in pace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Psalm 116</r>
§11.0a67a14e81
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Show us, O Lord, thy mercy.
<r>℟.</r> And grant us thy salvation.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>D</c>irect, we beseech thee, O Lord, our actions by thy holy inspiration, and carry them on by thy gracious assistance: that every prayer and work of ours may always begin from thee, and by thee be happily ended.
Through Christ our Lord.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Our help is ✠ in the name of the Lord,
<r>℟.</r> Who made heaven and earth.
<n>Si non sequitur aliqua Hora dicitur</n>
<r>℣.</r> May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, cuius providéntia in sui dispositióne non fállitur: te súpplices exorámus; ut nóxia cuncta submóveas, et ómnia nobis profutúra concédas.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.d0dc1258b5:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, Whose never-failing Providence ordereth all things both in heaven and earth, we humbly beseech thee to put away from us all hurtful things, and to give us those things which be profitable for us.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
